1.explanation:
• category-renderer.js is the module that renders each category’s clumps (passed/failed). It needs to detect when passed audits carry a `result.warnings` array and inject a new `.lh-warnings` node immediately after the `.lh-clump--passed` list.  
• templates.html holds the static markup templates for report sections. A new template snippet for the warnings block must be added so category-renderer can instantiate it.  
• html-report-assets.js contains the CSS rules for report elements. We need to define styling for the new `.lh-warnings` selector (orange border, padding, nested lists) to match the design mock.  
• util.js may need new helper functions (e.g. to convert a warnings array into a nested `<ul>`) or formatting utilities to render the warning text, so category-renderer’s implementation stays clean and consistent with other list renderers.
1.bug_scenario: In the Lighthouse HTML report, any audit that passes but still emits one or more warning messages is currently swallowed and never displayed in the “Passed audits” section. The expected behaviour is that immediately after the list of passed audits a distinct “Warnings:” block should appear (with class `.lh-warnings`), containing a nested bullet list of each warning from those audits.

2.explanation: The CategoryRenderer (lighthouse-core/report/html/renderer/category-renderer.js) is responsible for building each category’s DOM, including grouping passed audits. To implement the new warnings block, this file needs logic after rendering the .lh-clump--passed section to collect any ref.result.warnings from passed auditRefs and append a .lh-warnings container with the heading and nested list items. The templates.html file (lighthouse-core/report/html/templates.html) defines the report’s markup and CSS classes, so it must be updated with styling rules (e.g. border, padding, font) for the .lh-warnings element and markup hooks (like the “Warnings:” heading) that CategoryRenderer will instantiate. Together, these two files enable the UI change that surfaces passed‐audit warnings as specified by the test and design mockup.
2.bug_scenario: In the Lighthouse HTML report, any warnings emitted by audits that nevertheless passed (score=1) aren’t surfaced in the “Passed audits” section. The expected behavior is that immediately after the expanded “Passed audits” list there is a styled box (with class .lh-warnings) headed “Warnings:” containing a nested bullet list of all warning messages from those passed audits, as shown in the provided screenshot and exercised by the existing Jest test.
